newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close off as foreign bids stay away.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close off as foreign bids stay away.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off in low volume on a lack of market-moving local news and weak foreign interest, traders said.
"The market's hungry for news that will bring foreign investors back," said Multinvest broker Jose Gregorio Tineo.
The market's 19-share index closed down 1.12 percent at 6,172.08 points as 10.5 million shares traded, worth two billion bolivars ($4.2 million).
Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV meanwhile fell 1.16 percent to 94.70 points.
Telephone tariff increases, averaging 4.18 percent, were put in place today -- exactly a month after foreign investors were scared by apparent government reluctance to increase rates.
Trade in bellwether utility Electricidad de Caracas accounted for nearly a quarter of the session's total volume, the stock closing off 6.65 bolivars at 499.85.
Despite the share price drop, long due tariff hikes for the company are widely expected to be announced later this week, dealers said.
Venezuela's cabinet of economic ministers on Friday approved a framework to govern electricity tariff increases, though officials said higher rates would not be phased in until May.
